criteria.scenario: A dense admin worklist uses custom tab-like filters, a modal editor, sortable columns and inline validation. Automated axe checks are clean, but keyboard users can lose focus after closing the modal and custom tabs are plain divs with click handlers.
criteria.decision_to_make: Determine the accessibility verification and interaction changes required for the critical workflow.
must_do: prefer native semantics or implement complete ARIA/keyboard behavior
define modal focus entry/return behavior
verify keyboard operation manually
test validation/error associations
treat automation as partial evidence
must_not_do: declare accessibility complete from axe alone

criteria.scenario: On a 3200 px monitor the application keeps a narrow 1100 px centered column, forcing frequent horizontal/vertical navigation inside a dense worklist. A redesign proposes more cards, larger padding and stronger shadows to look 'premium'.
criteria.decision_to_make: Set visual hierarchy, density and wide-screen behavior grounded in the task.
must_do: use wide-screen space where it improves comparison
set intentional density for frequent operator work
prioritize hierarchy through spacing/type/alignment before decoration
preserve accessibility and semantic status cues
test realistic long/empty/error data
must_not_do: hide relevant columns solely to make screenshots cleaner

criteria.scenario: One feature team needs a table row with a special inline action and asks to add a new Core DataTable variant immediately. No other feature uses the behavior, and the variant would require a new focus/keyboard contract.
criteria.decision_to_make: Choose Local/Extended/Core scope and the evidence required for promotion.
must_do: evaluate semantic stability and actual reuse
keep one-off behavior local unless promotion criteria are met
define accessibility/behavior contract before promotion
assign ownership and migration/deprecation policy
use repeated overrides as feedback on abstraction quality
must_not_do: promote based only on visual similarity or hypothetical reuse
put product-specific business rules into a Core primitive

criteria.scenario: A worklist has q/school/subject/view/page/limit in the URL, but the implementation also copies them into local React state and synchronizes them through effects. Back navigation sometimes shows stale filters and duplicate fetches occur.
criteria.decision_to_make: Refactor state ownership and async behavior without creating another source of truth.
must_do: make URL the source of truth for navigational state where appropriate
derive values instead of duplicating state
use event-driven updates instead of effect chains
define loading/stale/error behavior for server state
test back/forward/shareable URL behavior
must_not_do: use effects for ordinary derived state
fix symptoms with arbitrary timing guards
